To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the level of the public sector's involvement in health care systems is significantly and negatively associated with the attainment of macro-economic efficiency in health care, after controlling for other relevant factors".

(1) The level of public involvement in a health care system has a negative impact on macro-economic efficiency; (2) The level of private cost sharing in a health care financing system has a positive impact on macro-economic performance; (3) The higher the level of private cost-sharing, the more efficient the health care system is; and (4) The higher the public cost sharing, the less efficient the health care financing system is.
(1) The macro-economic efficiency of a health care system is associated with the level of public involvement in the health sector, as well as the degree of public cost sharing.

the following issues: 1) the association between the health care system and the attainment of health care policy goals, such as equity, efficiency and accessibility, and 2) the relationship between the health care expenditure and the health care system, especially in terms of the level of public involvement.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more public involvement there is, the better the health policy goals are achieved.
a higher level of public sector participation in a health care system may be more efficient in terms of the macro-economic goals of the health care system.
the health policy goals of equity, cost-containment and efficiency are mutually compatible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the macro-economic efficiency in health care is influenced by the system factors such as the Public to Total Expenditure Ratio (PTE), Coverage Rate (CR) and Public Cost Sharing (PCS).
the health care system factors, such as public sector involvement and public-private mix, are important for the attainment of health care goals, including macro-economic efficiency.
the macro-economic efficiency and the equity of the health care system are positively associated with one another.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the macro-economic efficiency in health care is associated with the level of public involvement in the system, and that this association may be more pronounced in developing countries than in developed countries.
health care systems that are highly reliant on public financing and that have low levels of public cost-sharing have higher macro-economic efficiency.
the macro-economic efficiency is not necessarily sacrificed in order to attain higher equity and accessibility.
